{{Wiktionary|thousand|1000}}

'''1000''' or '''one thousand''' is the [[natural number]] following [[999 (number)|999]] and preceding [[1001 (number)|1001]]. In most [[English-speaking countries]], it can be written with or without a [[comma]] or sometimes a period [[decimal mark#Digit grouping|separating]] the thousands [[Numerical digit|digit]]: '''1,000'''.

A group of one thousand units is sometimes known, from [[Ancient Greek]], as a '''chiliad'''.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/chiliad|title=chiliad|publisher=[[Merriam-Webster]]}}</ref> A period of one thousand years may be known as a chiliad or, more often from [[Latin]], as a [[millennium]]. The number 1000 is also sometimes described as a '''short thousand''' in medieval contexts where it is necessary to distinguish the [[Germanic languages|Germanic]] concept of 1200 as a [[long thousand]]. It is the first 4-digit [[integer]].

== Notation ==

* The decimal representation for one thousand is
** '''1000'''—a [[1|one]] followed by three [[0|zeros]], in the general notation;
** '''1 × 10<sup>3</sup>'''—in [[engineering notation]], which for this number coincides with:
** '''1 × 10<sup>3</sup>''' exactly—in [[scientific notation|scientific normalized exponential notation]];
** '''1 E+3''' exactly—in [[scientific notation#E notation|scientific E notation]].
* The [[SI prefix]] for a thousand units is "[[kilo-]]", abbreviated to "k"—for instance, a [[kilogram]] or "kg" is a thousand [[gram]]s. This is sometimes extended to non-SI contexts, such as "ka" ([[kiloannum]]) being used as a shorthand for periods of 1000 years. In [[computer science]], however, "kilo-" is used more loosely to mean 2 to the 10th power (1024 or 2<sup>10</sup>).
* In the [[SI#SI writing style|SI writing style]], a [[non-breaking space]] can be used as a [[thousands separator]], i.e., to separate the digits of a number at every power of 1000.
* Multiples of thousands are occasionally represented by replacing their last three zeros with the letter "K" or "k": for instance, writing "$30k" for $30,000 or using "Y2K" to denote the [[Year 2000 problem|Year 2000 computer problem]].
* A thousand units of [[currency]], especially [[dollar]]s or [[Pound (currency)|pound]]s, are colloquially called a ''grand''. In the United States, this is sometimes abbreviated with a "G" suffix.

== In mathematics ==
A '''[[chiliagon]]''' is a 1000-sided [[polygon]].<ref name="Chilia">{{Cite OEIS|A195163|1000-gonal numbers: a(n) equal to n*(499*n - 498)}}</ref>

== Numbers in the range 1001–1999 ==

=== 1001 to 1099 ===

==== 1001 ====
{{Main|1001 (number)}}

==== 1002 ====
{{main|1002 (number)}}

==== 1004 ====
'''1004''' = 2<sup>2</sup> × 251. It is a [[heptanacci number]].<ref name="Heptanacci numbers">{{Cite OEIS|A122189|Heptanacci numbers}}</ref>

==== 1009 ====
'''1009''' is the smallest four-digit [[prime number|prime]], a [[Lucky prime#Lucky primes|Lucky prime]], and [[Chen prime]]. It is [[palindromic number|palindromic]] in bases 11, 15, 19, 24 and 28: (838<sub>11</sub>, 474<sub>15</sub>, 2F2<sub>19</sub>, 1I1<sub>24</sub>, 181<sub>28</sub>).

==== 1011 ====
'''1011''' = 3 × 337.  It is a [[Harshad number]] in bases 5, 10, 15, 20, 25, 30, 35, 40, 45, 50, 55, 60, 65, 70, 75 (and 202 other bases). It is the largest natural number ''n'' such that 2<sup>n</sup> contains 101 and does not contain 11011. There are 1011 partitions of 1 into reciprocals of positive integers <= 16 [[Egyptian fraction]].<ref name="A020473">{{cite OEIS|A020473|2=Egyptian fractions: number of partitions of 1 into reciprocals of positive integers <= n}}</ref>

==== 1013 ====
'''1013''' is a prime number, a [[Sophie Germain prime]],<ref name="Sophie Germain">{{Cite OEIS|A005384|Sophie Germain primes p: 2p+1 is also prime}}</ref> and a [[centered square number]],<ref name="Centered square numbers">{{Cite OEIS|A001844|Centered square numbers}}</ref> 

==== 1016 ====
'''1016''' = 2<sup>3</sup> × 127. It is [[stella octangula number]] and a member of the [[Mian–Chowla sequence]].<ref name="Mian-Chowla">{{Cite OEIS|A005282|Mian-Chowla sequence}}</ref> There are 1016 surface points on a cube with edge-length 14.<ref name="A005897">{{cite OEIS|A005897|6*n^2 + 2 for n > 0}}</ref>

==== 1019 ====
'''1019''' is a [[Sophie Germain prime]],<ref name="Sophie Germain" /> a [[safe prime]],<ref name="Safe primes">{{Cite OEIS|A005385|Safe primes p: (p-1)/2 is also prime}}</ref> and a [[Chen prime]].

==== 1021 ====
'''1021''' is a [[Lucky number#Lucky primes|Lucky prime]] and a [[twin prime]] with '''1019'''.

==== 1023 ====
{{Main|1023 (number)}}

==== 1024 ====
{{Main|1024 (number)}}

==== 1025 ====
'''1025''' = 5<sup>2</sup> × 41. It is a [[Jacobsthal-Lucas number]] and the hypotenuse of a [[primitive Pythagorean triangle]]. It is a [[Proth number]] because 1025 = 2<sup>10</sup> + 1. It is a member of the [[Moser–de Bruijn sequence]] because its base-4 representation (100001<sub>4</sub>) contains only digits 0 and 1, or equivalently,  it's a sum of distinct powers of 4 (4<sup>5</sup> + 4<sup>0</sup>).

==== 1028 ====
'''1028''' = 2<sup>2</sup> × 257. It is sum of totient function for first 58 integers.

==== 1029 ====
There are 1029 primes <= 2<sup>13</sup>.<ref name="auto3">{{cite OEIS|A007053|2=Number of primes <= 2^n}}</ref>

==== 1031 ====
'''1031''' is a prime number, a [[Sophie Germain prime]],<ref name="Sophie Germain" /> a [[super-prime]], and a [[Chen prime]]. It is the exponent and number of ones for the fifth base-10 [[repunit|repunit prime]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A004023|Indices of prime repunits: numbers n such that 11...111 (with n 1's)... is prime}}</ref>

==== 1033 ====
'''1033''' is a prime number and an [[emirp]]. It forms a [[twin prime]] pair with '''1031.'''

==== 1035 ====
'''1035''' = 3<sup>2</sup> × 5 × 23. It is a [[hexagonal number]]<ref name="Hexagonal number">{{Cite OEIS|A000384|Hexagonal numbers}}</ref> and the 45th [[triangular number]].<ref name="Triangular number">{{Cite OEIS|A000217|Triangular numbers}}</ref>

==== 1039 ====
'''1039''' is a [[Chen prime]] and a [[Lucky prime]]. There are 1039 partitions of 30 that do not contain 1 as a part.<ref name="auto8">{{cite OEIS|A002865|Number of partitions of n that do not contain 1 as a part}}</ref>

==== 1040 ====
'''1040''' = 2<sup>4</sup> × 5 × 13. There are 1040 pieces that could be seen in a 6 × 6 × 6 × 6 Rubik's Tesseract.

==== 1046 ====
'''1046''' = 2 × 523. It is a coefficient of f(q), the 3rd order mock theta function.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A000025|Coefficients of the 3rd-order mock theta function f(q)}}</ref>

==== 1049 ====
'''1049''' is a prime number, a [[Sophie Germain prime]],<ref name="Sophie Germain" /> a [[highly cototient number]],<ref name="highly cototient">{{Cite OEIS|A100827|Highly cototient numbers: records for a(n) in A063741}}</ref> and a [[Chen prime]].

==== 1051 ====
'''1051''' is a prime number, a [[centered pentagonal number]],<ref name="Centered pentagonal">{{Cite OEIS|A005891|Centered pentagonal numbers}}</ref> and a [[centered decagonal number]].

==== 1056 ====
'''1056''' = 2<sup>5</sup> × 3 × 11. It is a [[pronic number]].<ref name="pronic number">{{Cite OEIS|A002378|Oblong (or promic, pronic, or heteromecic) numbers}}</ref>

==== 1060 ====
'''1060''' = 2<sup>2</sup> × 5 × 53. It is the sum of the first twenty-five primes from [[2]] through [[97 (number)|97]] (the number of primes less than [[100]])<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A007504|Sum of the first n primes}}</ref> and the sixth sum of 10 consecutive primes, starting with [[23 (number)|23]] through [[131 (number)|131]].<ref name="auto102">{{Cite OEIS|A127337|Numbers that are the sum of 10 consecutive primes}}</ref>

==== 1061 ====
'''1061''' is a prime number, an [[emirp]], and a [[twin prime]] with '''1063.''' There are 1061 prime numbers between 1000 and [[10000 (number)|10000]] (or, number of four-digit primes in [[decimal]] representation).<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A006879|Number of primes with n digits.}}</ref>

==== 1063 ====
'''1063''' is a prime number, a [[super-prime]], a [[twin prime]] with '''1061''', and the sum of seven consecutive primes (137 + 139 + 149 + 151 + 157 + 163 + 167)

==== 1069 ====
'''1069''' is a prime number and an [[emirp]].<ref name="auto4">{{Cite OEIS|A006567|Emirps (primes whose reversal is a different prime)}}</ref>

==== 1076 ====
'''1076''' = 2<sup>2</sup> × 269. There are 1076 strict trees weight 11.<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A273873|Number of strict trees of weight n}}</ref>

==== 1078 ====
'''1078''' = 2 × 7<sup>2</sup> × 11. It is an [[Euler number|Euler]] transform of negative [[integers]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A073592|Euler transform of negative integers}}</ref>

==== 1080 ====
'''1080''' = 2<sup>3</sup> × 3<sup>3</sup> × 5. It is a pentagonal number<ref name="Pentagonal number">{{Cite OEIS|A000326|Pentagonal numbers}}</ref> and a [[largely composite number]].<ref name="OEIS-A067128">{{Cite OEIS|A067128|Ramanujan's largely composite numbers}}</ref>

==== 1081 ====
'''1081''' = 23 × 47. It is the 46th [[triangular number]]<ref name="Triangular number" /> and a member of [[Padovan sequence]].<ref name="Padovan sequence">{{Cite OEIS|A000931|Padovan sequence}}</ref>

==== 1086 ====
'''1086''' = 2 × 3 × 181. It is a [[Smith number]]<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A006753|Smith numbers}}</ref> and the sum of totient function for the first 59 integers.

==== 1087 ====
'''1087''' is a prime number, a super-prime, a [[cousin prime]], and a [[lucky prime]].<ref>{{Cite OEIS|A031157|Numbers that are both lucky and prime}}</ref>

==== 1089 ====
{{Main|1089 (number)}}

==== 1091 ====
'''1091''' is a prime number, a [[cousin prime]], and a [[twin prime]] with '''1093.'''

==== 1093 ====
1093 is a [[twin prime]] with '''1091.'''  Together with 1091 and 1097, it forms a [[prime triplet]]. It is a [[happy prime]] and a [[star prime|star]]<ref name="Centered 12-gonal numbers">{{Cite OEIS|A003154|Centered 12-gonal numbers. Also star numbers}}</ref> [[star prime|prime]]. It is also the smallest [[Wieferich prime]]. 1093 is a [[repunit prime]] in base&#x20;3 because:

: <math>1093 = 1111111_3 = 3^6 + 3^5 + 3^4 + 3^3 + 3^2 + 3^1 + 3^0 = \frac{3^7-1}{2} \, .</math>

==== 1097 ====
'''1097''' is a prime number, an [[emirp]],<ref name="auto4" /> and a [[Chen prime]].

'''1103''' is a prime number, a [[Sophie Germain prime]],<ref name="Sophie Germain" /> and a [[balanced prime]].<ref name="Balanced prime">{{Cite OEIS|A006562|Balanced primes}}</ref>

'''1104''' = 2<sup>4</sup> × 3 × 23. It is a [[Keith number]]<ref name="Keith number">{{Cite OEIS|A007629|Repfigit (REPetitive FIbonacci-like diGIT) numbers (or Keith numbers)}}</ref>

'''1118''' = 2 × 13 × 43. There are 1118 [[Unimodular matrix|unimodular]] 2 × 2 matrices having all terms in {0,1,...,21}.<ref name="auto54">{{cite OEIS|A210000|Number of unimodular 2 X 2 matrices having all terms in {0,1,...,n}<nowiki />}}</ref>

'''1128''' =  2<sup>3</sup> × 3 × 47. It is the 47th [[triangular number]]<ref name="Triangular number" /> and the 24th hexagonal number.<ref name="Hexagonal number" /> 1128 is the dimensional representation of the largest [[vertex operator algebra]] with [[central charge]] of 24, ''D''<sub>24</sub>.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Van Ekeren |first1=Jethro |last2=Lam |first2=Ching Hung |last3=Möller |first3=Sven |last4=Shimakura |first4=Hiroki |title=Schellekens' list and the very strange formula |journal=[[Advances in Mathematics]] |volume=380 |publisher=[[Elsevier]] |location=Amsterdam |year=2021 |article-number=107567 |doi=10.1016/j.aim.2021.107567 |doi-access=free |mr=4200469 |zbl=1492.17027 |s2cid=218870375 |arxiv=2005.12248 }}</ref>

'''1151''' is the first prime number following a [[prime gap]] of 22.<ref name="Prime gap">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A000101|title=Sloane's A000101 : Increasing gaps between primes (upper end)|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-07-10}}</ref> It is also a [[Chen prime]].

==== 1152 ====
'''1152''' = 2<sup>7</sup> × 3<sup>2</sup>. It is a [[highly totient number]],<ref name="highly totient">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A097942|title=Sloane's A097942 : Highly totient numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-12}}</ref> a [[3-smooth]] number, and an [[Achilles number]].

==== 1153 ====
'''1153''' is a [[super-prime]] and a [[Proth prime]].<ref name="Proth prime">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A080076|title=Sloane's A080076 : Proth primes|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-12}}</ref>

==== 1159 ====
'''1159''' = 19 × 61. It is a [[centered octahedral number]]<ref name="auto7">{{cite OEIS|A001845|Centered octahedral numbers (crystal ball sequence for cubic lattice)|access-date=2022-06-02}}</ref>  and a member of the Mian–Chowla sequence.<ref name="Mian-Chowla" />

==== 1160 ====
'''1160''' = 2<sup>3</sup> × 5 × 29. It is an [[octagonal number]].<ref name="auto17">{{cite OEIS|A000567|Octagonal numbers: n*(3*n-2). Also called star numbers}}</ref>

'''1161''' = 3<sup>3</sup> × 43. It is the sum of the first twenty-six primes.

'''1169''' = 7 × 167. It is a highly cototient number<ref name="highly cototient" />

'''1171''' is a super-prime.{{Citation needed|date=April 2026}}

'''1182''' = 2 × 3 × 197. There are 1182 necklaces possible with 14 beads of 2 colors (that cannot be turned over).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A000031|title=A000031 - OEIS|website=oeis.org}}</ref>

'''1191''' = 3 × 397 = 35<sup>2</sup> - 35 + 1 = H<sub>35</sub>, the 35th Hogben number.<ref name="auto77">{{cite OEIS|A002061|Central polygonal numbers: n^2 - n + 1}}</ref>

[[oeis:A059801|4<sup>1193</sup> - 3<sup>1193</sup> is prime]].

=== 1200 to 1299 ===

==== 1200 ====
'''1200''' = 2<sup>4</sup> × 3 × 5<sup>2</sup>. There are 1200 households in the [[Nielsen ratings]] sample.<ref>Meehan, Eileen R., ''Why TV is not our fault: television programming, viewers, and who's really in control'' Lanham, MD: Rowman & Littlefield, 2005</ref> 

1200 is known as the '''[[long thousand]]''' or ten "[[long hundred]]s" of 120 each. It is the traditional reckoning of large numbers in [[Germanic languages]].

==== 1201 ====
'''1201''' is a [[super-prime]], a centered square number,<ref name="Centered square numbers" /> and a [[centered decagonal number]].

==== 1202 ====
'''1202''' = 2 × 601. There are a maximum of 1202 [https://mathworld.wolfram.com/PlaneDivisionbyEllipses.html regions when the plane is divided by 25 ellipses].<ref name="auto91">{{cite OEIS|A051890|2*(n^2 - n + 1)}}</ref>

'''1203''' = 3 × 401. It is the smallest number greater than 1000 in the coordinating sequence for the (2,6,∞) tiling of the hyperbolic plane.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A265070|title=A265070 - OEIS|website=oeis.org}}</ref>

==== 1204 ====
'''1204''' = 2<sup>2</sup> × 7 × 43. It is the magic constant for a 7 × 7 × 7 magic cube.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://number.academy/1204|title=1204 (number)|website=The encyclopedia of numbers}}</ref>

==== 1205 ====
'''1205''' = 5 × 241. There are 1205 partitions of 28 such that the number of odd parts is a part<ref name="auto72">{{cite OEIS|A240574|Number of partitions of n such that the number of odd parts is a part}}</ref>

==== 1207 ====
'''1207''' = 17 × 71. It is a composite [[de Polignac number]].<ref name="auto53">{{cite OEIS|A098237|Composite de Polignac numbers}}</ref>

==== 1208 ====
'''1208''' = 2<sup>3</sup> × 151. There are 1208 strict chains of divisors starting with the superprimorial A006939(3).<ref>{{cite OEIS|A337070|Number of strict chains of divisors starting with the superprimorial A006939(n)}}</ref>

==== 1210 ====
'''1210''' = 2 × 5 × 11<sup>2</sup>. It is an amicable number with 1184<ref>Higgins, ibid.</ref> and a [[Self-descriptive number]].

==== 1211 ====
'''1211''' = 7 × 173. It is a composite [[de Polignac number]]<ref name="auto53" />

==== 1212 ====
'''1212''' = 2<sup>2</sup> × 3 × 101 = <math>\sum_{k=0}^{17} p(k)</math>, where <math>p(k)</math> is the number of partitions of <math>k</math>.<ref>{{cite OEIS|A000070|Sum_{0..n} A000041(k)}}</ref>

==== 1213 ====
'''1213''' is a prime number and an [[emirp]].

==== 1214 ====
'''1214''' = 2 × 607. It is a spy number and the sum of the first 39 composite numbers.<ref name="auto94">{{cite OEIS|A053767|Sum of first n composite numbers}}</ref>

'''1215''' = 3<sup>5</sup> × 5. There are 1215 edges in the [[:File:Hexagonal triangle.png|hexagonal triangle]] T(27)<ref name="auto60">{{cite OEIS|A140091|3*n*(n + 3)/2}}</ref>

'''1216''' = 2<sup>6</sup> × 19. It is a nonagonal number<ref name="Nonagonal number">{{Cite web|url=https://oeis.org/A001106|title=Sloane's A001106 : 9-gonal (or enneagonal or nonagonal) numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-12}}</ref>

'''1219''' = 23 × 53. It is a [[centered triangular number]]<ref name="auto52">{{cite OEIS|A005448|Centered triangular numbers: 3n(n-1)/2 + 1}}</ref> and a zero of [[Mertens function]].

'''1220''' = 2<sup>2</sup> × 5 × 61. It is a zero of Mertens function. There are 1220 binary vectors of length 16 containing no singletons.<ref name="auto50">{{cite OEIS|A006355|Number of binary vectors of length n containing no singletons}}</ref>

Also centered octagonal numbers|website=The On-Line Encyclopedia of Integer Sequences|publisher=OEIS Foundation|access-date=2016-06-12}}</ref> a 29-gonal number,<ref>{{cite OEIS|A303815|Generalized 29-gonal (or icosienneagonal) numbers}}</ref> a 60-gonal number,<ref>{{cite OEIS|A249911|60-gonal (hexacontagonal) numbers}}</ref> and a 124-gonal number. It is the sum of 5 consecutive odd cubes:

1225 = 1<sup>3</sup> + 3<sup>3</sup> + 5<sup>3</sup> + 7<sup>3</sup> + 9<sup>3</sup>.

Also enumerates permutations by their major index}}</ref>

1453

==== 1458 ====
'''1458''' = 2 × 3<sup>6</sup>. It is the [[Hadamard's maximal determinant problem|maximum determinant]] of an 11 by 11 matrix of zeroes and ones<ref>{{citation
 |last=Hadamard|first=J.|title=Résolution d'une question relative aux déterminants|journal=Bulletin des Sciences Mathématiques|volume=17|pages=240–246|year=1893}}</ref> and a [[3-smooth]] number.  

1458 is one of three numbers which, when its base 10 digits are added together, produces a sum which, when multiplied by its reversed self, yields the original number:
: 1 + 4 + 5 + 8 = 18
: 18 × 81 = 1458  
: The only other non-trivial numbers with this property are [[81 (number)|81]] and [[1729 (number)|1729]], as well as the trivial solutions [[1 (number)|1]] and [[0 (number)|0]]. It was proven by [[Masahiko Fujiwara]]. <ref>{{citation
 |last=Fujiwara|first=M.|title=Introduction to Truly Beautiful Mathematics|pages=100–101|year=2005}}</ref>
